clue.text: Broadcaster, after great effort, getting hold of verse composer

indicators.note: the broadcaster comes after the effort in the answer
the effort word grips the verse letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a great effort is a strain
Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: A broadcaster strains to get hold of some verse by a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky was the Russian-born composer of The Rite of Spring.

clue.text: Model English station

parts.note: to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: A model English railway station, as in a toy train set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like an adjective for the station but is a verb: to pose for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A station is a place where something is positioned, a location or spot.

clue.text: Actress Peggy supporting on stage again

indicators.note: in a down clue the actress sits below, holding up the other piece

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
Peggy Mount was an English comic actress known for battleaxe roles

explanation.surface: Peggy Mount playing a supporting part on stage once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Peggy Mount (1915-2001) was a British stage and TV actress.
explanation.definitionFit: To remount a play is to put on a production of it once more.

clue.text: Blissful place — coppers for hard Australian wine

indicators.note: the police go in place of the two letters, standing for them

parts.note: Valhalla is the hall of the slain heroes in Norse myth, a heaven
H for hard (pencils) and A for Australian
coppers are the police

explanation.surface: Australian police swap a blissful place for a hard wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts POLICE where H and A stood in VALHALLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Valpolicella is a red wine from the Veneto region of Italy.

clue.text: Having nothing on suspect seen nicked by detective with new uniform on

indicators.note: in a down clue the new uniform letters sit on top of the rest

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are caught inside the detective's abbreviation

parts.note: DS is a detective sergeant

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, signalling a reworking of the letters of seen

explanation.surface: A naked suspect is arrested by a detective in a new uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like the person arrested but is the anagram signal, making ENES; 'nicked by' is police slang for arrested, here meaning held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudeness is nakedness, the state of wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Heard line of people and what they do in country

indicators.note: heard tells us the words are spoken, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.words: line of people and what they do
parts.note: a line of people is a queue, and what people in a queue do is wait

explanation.surface: Someone reports hearing about queues and waiting in some country.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuwait is a small oil-rich state at the head of the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Bit of mashed potato maybe sweetheart's passed back

indicators.note: passed back means the letters are handed over in the opposite direction

parts.note: a sweetheart is a pet, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A spoonful of mashed potato is passed back by a sweetheart at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mashed Potato is a 1960s dance craze, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance such as the Mashed Potato is made up of individual moves, each one a step.

clue.text: With armband short, abruptly vacated seaside resort

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: a torque is a twisted metal band worn on the neck or arm

indicators.note: vacated means the word is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly leaves a seaside resort with a short armband.
explanation.walkthrough: TORQUAY is a resort on the Devon coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquay is a well-known holiday town on the English Riviera in Devon.

clue.text: Old soap actress at pub, drunken one in pictures

indicators.note: in places the inner pieces inside the outer word

parts.note: pix is slang for pictures
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: drunken signals that the letters of one stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A former soap star at the pub, drunk, appears in the photos.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat Phoenix played Elsie Tanner in the British TV soap Coronation Street. 'drunken' turns ONE into OEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat Phoenix was an actress in the long-running ITV serial Coronation Street, a famous soap.

clue.text: Collapsed private is unstable

parts.note: to collapse is to tumble
private means belonging to oneself, one's own

explanation.surface: A soldier collapses because he is unsteady on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like the soldier but means personal, as in one's own.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilapidated building close to falling apart is ramshackle and shaky.

clue.text: Worry reflects interference to some extent

indicators.note: reflects means the letters are mirrored, read the other way
to some extent means only part of the word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Worry mirrors a degree of interference in one's life.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious and agitated over something.

clue.text: Book twice to meet nucleus of crew in operation of aircraft — BA, for example

indicators.note: in places the inner pieces inside the outer word

parts.note: aviation is the operating of aircraft

indicators.note: twice means the letter standing for book appears two times in a row
the nucleus is the core, the middle letters of crew

explanation.surface: Pictures British Airways crew booking flights.
explanation.walkthrough: BA looks like British Airways, fitting the aircraft surface, but is the short form of Bachelor of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: BA is a shortened form of a longer title, so it is an example of a contraction of words.

clue.text: Regularly fuzzy when getting in rounds — of this booze?

indicators.note: getting in places the picked letters inside the two circle letters

parts.note: rounds are O shapes, two letter Os

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Drinkers buying rounds of a booze get regularly fuzzy-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouzo is a Greek aniseed-flavoured spirit, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Cleaner's upset, overwhelmed by extra career

indicators.note: the upset word is engulfed by the extra's letters

parts.note: NB is no ball, an extra run in cricket
an upset is a minor illness, an ail
to career is to rush headlong

explanation.surface: A cleaner is upset at being swamped by extra work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner's' is Cleaner is. 'extra' is a cricket term: NB is a no ball, which gives the batting side an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stiff-bristled brush for scrubbing under the fingertips is a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Tot unfortunately worse before getting right herbal remedy

indicators.note: the scrambled letters come before the abbreviation for right

parts.note: to tot up is to add

indicators.note: unfortunately signals the letters of worse fall badly into a new order

explanation.surface: A child's health worsens before a herbal remedy puts things right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns WORSE into ERSWO. 'Tot' looks like a child but is the verb to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Adder's-wort is an old name for bistort, a plant once used in herbal medicine against snakebite.

clue.text: Party without alcohol and ties to be worn — most crazy

parts.note: a do is a party
TT means teetotal, abstaining from drink

indicators.note: worn suggests the letters of ties are battered out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dry party with ties to be worn sounds the craziest idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be worn' rearranges TIES into IEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty means mildly mad or eccentric, so the superlative is maddest.

clue.text: Sexual centre discussed barrier method?

indicators.note: discussed means spoken about, so a word that is said aloud

parts.note: the groin is the region of the body around the genitals

explanation.surface: A sex-education talk on barrier contraception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrier method' suggests condoms, keeping the sexual surface; the question mark flags that this barrier is a coastal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a low wall built out from a beach, a barrier used as a method of stopping erosion.

clue.text: Scotsman's stuck inside largely unable to shift periodical

indicators.note: the Scotsman is wedged inside the rearranged letters
to shift means the letters are moved around
largely means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman stuck inside is largely unable to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts UNABLE to UNABL, which 'to shift' rearranges to BNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something biannual happens twice a year, so it recurs at regular periods.

clue.text: Teacher preferring Spain for initial holiday

indicators.note: preferring means one letter is chosen over another, a swap
for initial says the swap happens to the opening letter

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher, a master
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A teacher would rather spend the spring holiday in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival in spring, a public holiday in many countries.

clue.text: Soldier's wearing something fireproof in US city

indicators.note: the soldier is clothed in the outer word, so it sits inside

parts.note: a safe is a strongbox built to withstand fire
a soldier ant is a type of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier in fireproof gear at work in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier's' is Soldier is; the soldier is the insect, not a fighting man.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the state capital of New Mexico.

clue.text: One in Glasgow area redirected cool Italian chap

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: Govan is a district of Glasgow on the Clyde
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: redirected means sent the other way, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: in means cool or fashionable

explanation.surface: An Italian man, redirected cool as anything in Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal: the I goes into GOVAN. GOVAN is a district of Glasgow, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni is the Italian equivalent of the man's name John.

clue.text: Ignore a stanza, when holding course in poetry

indicators.note: holding means the words contain the letters within them

explanation.surface: Advice to skip a stanza while studying a course in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course in poetry' looks like a class but is a heading on a compass, in its poetic spelling nor'-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor'-east is the poetic or nautical contraction of north-east, a compass direction to steer by.

clue.text: Fast food urge? Half repeatedly avoided this perhaps

indicators.note: half repeatedly means the back half of each of the words in turn is taken

explanation.surface: An urge for fast food, but someone avoided it half the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' points to burgers, but the second halves of Fast, food and urge are what count.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, filling food like suet pudding is the sort of thing a dieter steers clear of.

clue.text: Fault by leader in game to reveal playing card

indicators.note: by means next to, placing pieces side by side

parts.note: a sin is a moral fault

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word

parts.note: to let on is to reveal

explanation.surface: A game leader's fault is revealed by a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a singleton is the only card held in a suit.

clue.text: In US, fancy track being uneven

parts.note: aw is an American exclamation of surprise, like the British 'fancy!'
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: In America, a fancy racetrack that is bumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' is the exclamation of surprise, as in 'Fancy that!'
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew or crooked is out of line, not level.

clue.text: Wife spikes bird to be carved

indicators.note: the wife letter pierces the bird, getting inside it

parts.note: a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: A wife spits a bird ready for carving.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn means cut or shaped with blows of an axe or chisel.

clue.text: Love mate's jewellery

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: A lover's partner's jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate's' is mate is.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone set in rings and brooches.

clue.text: Advert by old German, describing tart, about to get award

indicators.note: by means next to, placing pieces side by side

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement

indicators.note: describing means drawing around, so the German word goes round the other

parts.note: the Jutes were an ancient Germanic people

indicators.note: about means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: acid means sharp or tart in taste

explanation.surface: An advert by an old German about a tart wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry but is the adjective sharp; 'about' reverses it to DICA, and 'describing' means drawing a line round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjudicate is to judge formally, and to award is to grant a judgement.

clue.text: Level match, when taking rook

indicators.note: taking means the match acquires the chess letter at its end

parts.note: a tie is a cup match
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A level chess match when a rook is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one row or layer in a stacked arrangement, a stage.

clue.text: Piece of garden heather not upsetting dog

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden
ling is a common heather

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, reading the word backwards

explanation.surface: A dog in a garden plot is not upsetting the heather.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bedlington terrier is a breed of English terrier with a lamb-like look.
